findings.title: Blocked addresses can be bypassed by changing letter case
findings.body: This lookup compares the submitted email to the stored address exactly, but email domains are case-insensitive and the application otherwise normalizes email addresses for lookup. If `blocked@example.com` is listed, a user can sign up with `blocked@EXAMPLE.COM` and avoid the block. Normalize both the stored address and lookup value, or make the comparison case-insensitive.

findings.title: Concurrent matches can lose statistics increments
findings.body: The method reads `match_count`, increments it in Ruby, and saves the whole record. If two signup validations match the same blocked address concurrently, both can read the same count and write the same incremented value, so one match is lost. Use an atomic database increment (and update `last_match_at` atomically) if these statistics are expected to be accurate.
